back: A period of negative economic growth: real GDP falls, commonly for two consecutive quarters.

front: What are the two broad causes of recession?
back: A fall in total (aggregate) demand, or a fall in the quantity or quality of resources (a supply shock).

front: Give three demand-side causes of recession.
back: Falling consumer confidence; lower investment; cuts in government spending; falling exports; higher interest rates or taxes.

front: How does a recession affect workers?
back: Job losses and fewer hours (cyclical unemployment), smaller pay rises, loss of skills, emigration.

front: What usually happens to the budget deficit in a recession?
back: It widens: tax revenue falls while spending on support for the poor and unemployed rises.

front: Name three types of policy to promote growth.
back: Fiscal (spending and taxes), monetary (interest rates and money supply) and supply-side (training, infrastructure, incentives).

front: Give two limits of expansionary fiscal policy.
back: Wider budget deficit and debt; time lags; extra income saved or spent on imports; inflation at full capacity.

front: Why may lower interest rates not end a recession?
back: Low confidence means people and firms do not borrow; banks may not lend; time lags.

front: What is the main strength and the main limit of supply-side policy?
back: It raises productive capacity, so growth without inflation; but it takes years and can be costly.
